beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Kavya, and this video is about why data agents win with a better harness, not a bigger model. Quick note: the voice you're hearing is AI, Kokoro text-to-speech reading a script I wrote and checked. When a data agent gives a wrong answer, the reflex is to blame the model. So today I hold the model fixed and change only the harness.

props.segment: A Better Harness, Not a Bigger Model
props.command: My data agent returned a confident wrong answer. Everyone says: use a bigger model. Before I believe that, if I hold the model fixed and change only the harness, does the wrong answer still ship?
props.runningText: running the same SQL through two harnesses…
output: real harness: caught on try 1, right on try 2

beats.narration_text: Here's the idea: a bigger model rarely fixes a flaky data agent. The harness does. What it's allowed to see, what it runs, and whether anything checks the answer before you get it.

props.text:
A smarter data agent needs a bigger model.
What it sees, runs, and checks.
props.contextTitle: A Better Harness, Not a Bigger Model

beats.narration_text: Strip the word harness down and it's four plain parts. Tool contracts: what the agent may call, and what comes back. Scoped context: only the tables the question needs, not the whole warehouse. A verify loop that checks the answer before it ships. And state, so it remembers what already failed. Notice that none of the four is the model.

beats.narration_text: So I ran it. A small SQLite warehouse, one question: total revenue by region. The model here is a scripted stand-in, so both runs get exactly the same SQL. Thin harness first: all eight tables in context, run the query, return. It says East seven-twenty, West eight hundred. Zero checks ran. The true answer is four hundred and five hundred.

shot.visual_intent: Real terminal run of demo/harness_demo.py thin. Output lines are the script's verbatim stdout; the WRONG line carries the one highlight.

question + 'scripted stand-in, identical drafts' print dim
'context: full schema, 8 tables' prints
'answer: East: 720  West: 800' and 'checks run: 0' print
'ground truth ... -> answer WRONG' prints highlighted; all hold

out.text: question: What is total order revenue by region?
model: scripted stand-in, identical drafts in both runs
ground truth: East: 400  West: 500  -> answer WRONG

beats.narration_text: Same SQL, real harness. Context scoped to three tables, the query run on a read-only connection, then one check: revenue by region has to add up to total order revenue. Fifteen-twenty isn't nine hundred, so the check fails and says why: the join fans out on order items. That failure goes back as state, the retry passes, and only then does an answer ship.

shot.visual_intent: Real terminal run of demo/harness_demo.py real. Verbatim stdout; the CHECK FAILED line carries the one highlight, then the passing retry and the correct answer.

'try 1: CHECK FAILED: sum 1,520 != orders total 900; join fans out on order_items' prints highlighted
'try 2: check passed: sum 900 = orders total 900' prints
'answer: East: 400  West: 500' prints; all hold

beats.narration_text: To be fair, this isn't model size never matters. A harness can't create reasoning the model doesn't have; a hard, genuinely new analysis still needs a stronger model. And my demo scripted the model, so it shows the mechanism, not a benchmark. The claim is narrower: for the failures agents actually ship, the sloppy join and the skipped check, fix the harness first.

beats.narration_text: Recap. A harness is four parts: tool contracts, scoped context, a verify loop, and state. With the model held fixed, the thin harness shipped a wrong answer with zero checks, and the real harness caught it with one. The boundary: it fixes execution failures, not missing reasoning. So before you reach for a bigger model, ask whether anything checks the answer.

props.artifactTitle: Data Agents Win With a Better Harness
artifactLines: Harness = tool contracts + scoped context + a verify loop + state.
Model held fixed: thin harness shipped a wrong answer with 0 checks.
Real harness: one invariant check caught it; the retry was right.
Boundary: it fixes execution failures, not missing reasoning.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take your own data agent and ask Claude exactly this: look at my agent's last wrong answer. Was the model wrong, or did nothing check the answer before it shipped? Help me add one verification step. The part to watch is the check Claude proposes. Make it an invariant your data must satisfy, like totals that have to add up. Run it before you upgrade anything.
